heading: Introduction
text: A payment lands in a database. A minute later, three other systems want to know about it: fraud detection, a reporting store, a notification service. You can ask the database every few seconds what changed (polling), or you can read the one place where the database already writes down every change: its transaction log. That second approach is change data capture , or CDC. In this article I build a CDC pipeline from SAP/Sybase ASE to Apache Kafka , and I show you how to build it yourself. First we run a working pipeline on your own machine and watch real events appear. Then we rebuild the …

heading: The path of one change
text: Here is the whole journey in five stops. We will meet each one again later with real commands and output. The application commits a row change. ASE writes it to its transaction log first, before it counts as durable. RepAgent reads the log. RepAgent is a thread inside ASE. It is built to feed a Replication Server , and it sends changes in a text-like format called LTL (Log Transfer Language) over the TDS protocol. Our connector pretends to be that Replication Server. We register a fake server name, CDC_RS , in the ASE interfaces file and point it at the connector's port 11752 . RepAgent …

heading: What the pipeline promises, and what it does not
text: The promise is at-least-once delivery : no committed change is lost, even if the connector or the network fails in the middle. The price is that after a restart some changes can arrive again . Every event carries an id, source.oqid , that lets a consumer spot the repeat. The reliability section later demonstrates this with a restart and shows the duplicates it produces. I do not claim exactly-once delivery, because that would be a different (and harder) design.

heading: How to use this article
text: Read straight through for the full story, or jump to a section when something breaks. The section "Why is there no data?" is organised by symptom. Run everything. Every command here has a script in lab/ . Output blocks are real captures; the file they came from is linked under each one. Where I have not run something, I say not run . Skip ahead to build once you have seen the pipeline work. The build-along starts from an empty project and reaches the same result.

heading: Check yourself
text: 1. Why does the connector buffer rows instead of publishing each one as it arrives? RepAgent sends changes of transactions that are not committed yet, and some of them roll back. Publishing early would show consumers changes that never really happened. The connector publishes a transaction only after its COMMIT. 2. What does "at-least-once" mean for a consumer? Nothing committed is lost, but after a restart the same change can be delivered again. Consumers need to tolerate repeats, for example by remembering the source.oqid of events they have processed.

heading: Why the log matters
text: ASE keeps log records until RepAgent says it has delivered them. If the connector is down, the log grows. The lab database enables trunc log on chkpt so ASE can still trim the log up to the point we have acknowledged; the script sybase/03_log_threshold.sql adds a threshold that raises an alert before the log fills. In a real system you must watch this: a stuck connector can eventually fill the log.

heading: One more filter: the maintenance user
text: The setting database.maintenance.user (default cdc_maint ) names a login whose transactions RepAgent does not forward. In ordinary replication that login is the Replication Server's own writer, so its changes are not sent back in a loop. Here it is useful for the same reason: changes made by that login never appear in Kafka. I have not tested this setting in the lab ( not run ).

heading: Step 1. The listener RepAgent connects to
text: RepAgent can only send to "a Replication Server" named in the ASE interfaces file. Your listener pretends to be one. heading: Step 4. The event Kafka sees

The price is a possible duplicate, as the reliability section showed. You also package everything as one JAR with the Maven shade plugin, which is the plugin Kafka Connect loads. heading: Why exact decimals are strings
text: Numbers in JSON are usually read as 64-bit floating point. That cannot hold every numeric(18,4) or money value exactly, and money must not drift by a fraction of a cent. The connector therefore sends exact decimal types as strings and keeps their digits as ASE stored them: smallmoney -12.34 arrives as "-12.3400" , with the scale of the column. Convert them in your consumer with a decimal type, not a float. The same applies to a numeric primary key: the key in the first section is {"payment_id":"1"} , a string, because payment_id is numeric(18,0) . Watch out for bigint . The connector writes …

heading: Dates carry no time zone
text: Date and time values are written exactly as ASE holds them, with no zone or offset. The connector does not know the server's time zone, so a consumer must decide what zone those values mean. In the first section's output, created_at came from ASE's getdate() in the container's zone.

Environment-dependent values
text: Hostnames, ports, credentials, database names, topic names, paths and configuration properties, and what to change per environment.
keywords: environment deploy configuration properties values table

heading: ltl.listen.host
text: Leave 0.0.0.0 to listen on every interface of the connector's container or host, or give one address to restrict it. The database must be able to reach this address.

heading: ltl.listen.port
text: Any free port. It must equal the port in the CDC_RS entry of the database's interfaces file (set by sybase/start.sh); change both together, and open the port between the two hosts.

heading: ltl.username
text: Choose your own login name, and set the same name in sp_config_rep_agent (sybase/02_repagent.sql). It is only checked by the connector; it is not a database account.
keywords: environment value credential rs_user (labelled local test value)

heading: ltl.password
text: Use a real secret and keep it out of source control (for Kafka Connect use a config provider or a secret). Set the same value in sp_config_rep_agent. The lab leaves net password encryption off, which sends it in plain text.
keywords: environment value credential rs_password (labelled local test value)

heading: ltl.charset
text: Leave empty to follow the character set in the RepAgent login. Set a Java charset name only if the database sends text in a set that the login does not describe correctly.

heading: ltl.trace
text: Set true only while troubleshooting: it logs every LTL message, which is very verbose and can contain data.

heading: database.server.name
text: The value select @@servername returns on your server. It is part of the stored offset key and of every event, so changing it later starts a new offset.

heading: database.name
text: The database you replicate. A RepAgent for any other database is refused. It is also the middle part of every topic name.

heading: database.maintenance.user
text: The login whose transactions RepAgent must not forward (normally the replication maintenance user of your environment).

heading: topic.prefix
text: The first part of every topic name (prefix, database, table). Change it to fit your topic naming rules; consumers must use the same names.

heading: table.include.list
text: The tables to publish. A table must also be marked with sp_setreptable in the database. Empty means every marked table.

heading: queue.max.transactions
text: How many committed transactions may wait between RepAgent and Kafka. Raise it for bursty workloads (uses more memory), lower it to make RepAgent wait sooner.

heading: poll.max.records
text: The most records one poll returns to Kafka Connect.

heading: large.transaction.warn.rows
text: The number of rows in one open transaction at which a warning is logged. All rows of an open transaction are kept in memory.

heading: replication.server.name
text: The name of the interfaces entry and of the RepAgent rs servername setting. The connector uses it only in the messages it sends; keep all three the same.

heading: ltl.dump.dir
text: A Java system property (-Dltl.dump.dir=<directory>) that saves every message RepAgent sends. Use a directory the Connect process can write to, and only while investigating.

heading: connector.class
text: Do not change it: it names the connector class inside the JAR on the plugin path.

heading: tasks.max
text: Leave 1: the connector always starts exactly one task and ignores a larger value.

heading: connector.name
text: The name under which Kafka Connect knows the connector. It appears in the REST URLs and in the stored offset key; choose one per database.

heading: key.converter / value.converter
text: The format of the Kafka messages. The consumers must read the same format. The connector builds schemaless maps, so keep the JSON converter with schemas disabled unless you add schemas.

heading: key.converter.schemas.enable / value.converter.schemas.enable
text: Keep false: the connector does not provide schemas, and true would wrap every message in a schema envelope.

heading: errors.tolerance
text: none stops the task on the first error; all would skip failing records. Skipping records in a change data capture pipeline hides data loss, so decide deliberately.

heading: Kafka bootstrap servers
text: The address of your Kafka brokers as the Connect worker reaches them (host and port of a listener it can use). With TLS or SASL more settings are needed; the lab uses neither.

heading: Connect group id
text: One group id per Kafka Connect cluster; workers with the same id form one cluster.

heading: Connect internal topics
text: Names of the topics where Connect stores connector configurations, offsets (the connector's restart position) and status. Do not delete the offsets topic: it holds the position.

heading: Connect internal topic replication
text: Use 3 (or your cluster's standard) on a cluster with several brokers; 1 is only for the single-broker lab.

heading: Connect REST listener
text: The REST API address. Advertise the host name other workers and tools use; protect the API (it can reconfigure connectors), the lab binds it to localhost only.
keywords: environment value port http://0.0.0.0:8083, advertised as connect:8083

heading: Connect plugin path
text: The folder Connect scans for connector JARs. Put the connector JAR (one folder per plugin) there and restart the worker.

heading: Connect offset flush interval
text: How often Connect stores offsets. A shorter interval means fewer repeated events after a crash; a longer one means less load on Kafka.

heading: Sybase ASE published port
text: The database port for tools on your machine. In another environment the database is reached at its own host and port.

heading: Kafka published port
text: The Kafka port for programs on your machine (the containers use kafka:9092). Use your cluster's listeners elsewhere.

heading: Kafka web UI published port
text: Where the web UI answers. Do not publish it beyond localhost without authentication.

heading: Container names
text: The names the lab scripts use in docker exec. Rename them only together with the scripts that use them.
keywords: environment value host cdc-lab-sybase, cdc-lab-kafka, cdc-lab-connect, cdc-lab-kafka-ui

heading: Container host names
text: The names the containers use for each other on the Docker network. The interfaces entry CDC_RS points at connect; the connector reaches Kafka as kafka.
keywords: environment value host sybase, kafka, connect

heading: Sybase image settings
text: The sa password is the public default of the image: never use it outside the lab. In a real environment the database already exists and has its own administrator.
keywords: environment value credential SYBASE_USER=sa, SYBASE_PASSWORD=myPassword (public image default), SYBASE_DB=phoenix_test

heading: Sybase setup scripts folder
text: The folder the first-boot script reads the SQL files from. A real database is configured with the same statements by its administrator.

heading: Kafka node and roles
text: A single node does both jobs in the lab. A cluster uses separate controllers or several nodes; this is the Kafka administrator's decision.
keywords: environment value property node 1, broker and controller, quorum 1@kafka:9093

heading: Kafka listeners
text: The advertised listeners must be addresses the clients can reach. Production listeners use TLS and authentication; the lab does not (TLS was not run).
keywords: environment value port PLAINTEXT :9092, CONTROLLER :9093, PLAINTEXT_HOST :29092, all in plain text

heading: Kafka internal replication
text: Single-broker values. Use your cluster's replication settings (for example 3 and 2).
keywords: environment value property all 1, group rebalance delay 0

heading: Web UI cluster settings
text: Point them at your own Kafka and Connect addresses, if you use the web UI at all.
keywords: environment value host cluster local, brokers kafka:9092, Connect http://connect:8083

heading: Database devices
text: Your database already has its devices. Keep the log on its own device and size it for the time the connector may be down.
keywords: environment value path phoenix_data 1G at /opt/sybase/data/phoenix_data.dat, phoenix_log 512M at /opt/sybase/data/phoenix_log.dat

heading: Database accounts
text: Use your own accounts with the same minimal rights: the replication role for the RepAgent administration, and no table rights for it. Keep passwords out of source control.
keywords: environment value credential sa, cdc_admin, cdc_app (passwords generated into lab/env/.lab-secrets)

heading: Interfaces file and error log
text: Paths inside the database container. On your server find the interfaces file (sql.ini on Windows) and the server error log in the ASE installation.

heading: Demo topic
text: The topic is topic.prefix, database.name and the table name joined by dots, so it changes with them.

heading: kafka.version
text: The Kafka version the connector is compiled against. Use the version of the Kafka Connect worker that will load the JAR.

heading: maven.compiler.release
text: The Java version of the compiled classes. The Java runtime of the Kafka Connect worker must be at least this version.
